title: DECISION: bidirectional opt-out (no receipts sent = no receipts seen)
description: When receiptSharing=false, inbound Peer/receipt events carrying readAt are also suppressed from the owner's clients. This removes the asymmetric-information problem: if Alice opts out of broadcasting but still sees Bob's read times, she gains information without reciprocity, which creates an incentive to exploit the opt-out. By tying the two together, the protocol enforces a consistent social contract. The alternative of asymmetric opt-out (suppress outbound only) would make the preference semantically inconsistent and harder to explain to users. Bidirectionality also simplifies implementation: one boolean controls both directions for a given account.
